notes.meaning: People who pull away from community often do so to follow their own selfish desires. When someone isolates themselves, they end up rejecting sound advice and good judgment. God designed people to live together and learn from one another.

A foolish person has no real desire to learn the truth or grow in wisdom. Instead, they only care about spouting whatever thoughts enter their mind to look clever. Real learning requires listening, but a fool only wants to show off.

Wicked behavior brings dishonor along with it. When an ungodly person enters a room, they tend to treat good people and godly instruction with scorn. In the end, their sinful living brings shame and public disgrace upon themselves.

Wise speech comes from a deep, rich supply of truth within the heart. A wise person does not boast loudly, but their understanding never runs dry. Their spoken words flow out like a fresh, bubbling stream that refreshes everyone who listens.

It is wrong for a judge or leader to side with evil people because of wealth, power, or personal friendship. Giving an unfair advantage to the guilty robs the innocent person of fair justice. Every case should be decided honestly on its true merits, without favoritism.

A foolish person speaks rashly and constantly stirs up conflict. They butt into arguments that are none of their business and provoke others to anger. By their insulting talk, they invite physical punishment upon their own heads.

Careless words bring about the ruin of the one who speaks them. When a fool gets into trouble, their own speech becomes a trap that entangles their soul even further. An undisciplined tongue creates disasters from which a person cannot easily escape.

Gossip and whispered secrets taste sweet to those who love hearing scandalous stories. Listeners swallow these tales greedily, and the words sink deep into their minds and memories. Even though gossip seems harmless to the hearer, it secretly poisons relationships and ruins reputations.

Neglecting your daily duties causes as much damage as actively destroying property. The lazy worker allows things to fall apart, while the reckless waster throws wealth away. Both paths lead to the exact same poverty in the end.

The name of the Lord stands for God's personal character, his mighty power, and his covenant promises. When trouble comes, godly people run to him by faith and prayer just as a soldier flees to a high fort. In God's shelter, they are lifted above danger and kept completely safe.

Wealthy people often believe their money can protect them from every hardship in life. They view their bank accounts like high, thick stone walls surrounding a safe city. Yet that security exists only in their own imagination, because riches cannot rescue anyone from real disaster.

Arrogance regularly shows up right before a person experiences a terrible crash. Pride blinds people to their own flaws, so they refuse correction and march straight into failure. In contrast, those who remain humble before God and others will eventually be rewarded with honor.

Jumping to answer before hearing all the facts is both foolish and embarrassing. Impatient people often interrupt because they are too proud to listen carefully. A wise person takes time to understand the whole story before offering a judgment.

A brave, resilient human spirit can carry someone through physical sickness and outward pain. But when a person's inner spirit is broken by guilt, grief, or deep depression, all strength collapses. A crushed heart has no human remedy and must look to God for healing.

Sensible people know they never have enough knowledge, so they keep searching for more. Their heart is ready to take in the truth, while their ear listens carefully to good instruction. Real understanding grows when we combine an open ear with a willing heart.

Bringing a generous present or showing polite courtesy opens doors that were previously shut. In ancient times, people brought gifts when approaching a king or leader to gain a hearing. Thoughtful generosity clears a pathway for a person to be received by people of influence.

The first person to tell their side of a dispute always sounds convincing, because they only mention the facts that favor them. But when the other party steps forward and asks pointed questions, the weak spots in the story are exposed. Wise judges always wait to hear both sides before making a decision.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin Vulgate translation, this verse has often been applied to the sacrament of penance, teaching that a righteous person should be the first to accuse themselves in confession.

notes.meaning: Casting lots was an accepted ancient way of settling tough disputes by placing the final decision in God's hands. This practice prevented violent fights between powerful opponents who refused to give ground. When both sides agreed to accept the outcome from God, peace was quickly restored.

When a close relative or dear friend is deeply wronged, their hurt feelings turn into a fortress of defense. Because love between brothers is so strong, a betrayal between them produces very stubborn bitterness. Breaking down those walls of resentment is harder than conquering a heavily fortified city.

Everyone must live with the practical results of the words that come out of their mouth. Wholesome and honest speech brings peace to the conscience and good outcomes in life. In the same way, speaking harmful words will eventually fill a person's life with bitter trouble.

Human words have huge consequences, capable of causing great good or terrible harm. In court, a truthful witness can save an innocent life, while a false witness can cause an execution. Those who love to talk must remember that they will eat whatever fruit their speech produces.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern teachers take this verse literally to mean that human words carry supernatural power to create reality, allowing believers to speak health and wealth into existence.

notes.meaning: Finding a godly wife is one of the greatest blessings a man can receive in this life. Marriage provides lifelong companionship and mutual help, just as God planned in the beginning. Entering into a good marriage is a wonderful sign of the Lord's kind favor and providence.

Poor people understand their need, so they learn to speak politely and plead for help. By contrast, rich people often become proud and speak rudely because they think their wealth makes them untouchable. This proverb warns against the hardening effects of money and reminds us to treat others with gentle respect.

Surrounding yourself with a crowd of shallow acquaintances does not guarantee help in hard times and can lead to financial ruin. But having one genuinely faithful companion is worth far more than a room full of casual associates. Such a loyal friend will stick by your side through every trial, proving even closer than a blood brother.
